sourceOfTruth: red-snapshot.mjs seal()/verify() — the manifest is committed into the snapshot (the record) and filtered out of the post-seal delta (so the tree copy is transient); the repository's format gate (scripts/format-lib/git-tracked-paths.sh + pnpm prettier:check) is what the surviving copy breaks.

inventory.producer: seal() in .claude/skills/pair-workflow-red-verify/scripts/red-snapshot.mjs — the sole writer of .pair/red-snapshots/pr-<n>-<phase>.json (manifestPathFor, then `git add -- <manifest> …` + `git commit --no-verify`, lines 316-325). Its counterpart verify() filters that same path out of the post-seal delta (`path !== manifest`, line 381), which is what makes REMOVAL the intended end state rather than a tolerated one.
inputs: the repository tree at the base
the format gate's derived file set: git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard filtered by extension (scripts/format-lib/git-tracked-paths.sh)
representations: the manifest BLOB inside the snapshot commit — the durable record, read by `git show <snapshot>:<manifest>` (verify, line 343)
the manifest FILE at HEAD / in the working tree — transient, and the defect when it survives
the Pair-RED-Snapshot commit trailer's `manifest=` field, which names the path under both representations
consumers: red-snapshot.mjs verify / verify-chain (read the blob from the snapshot commit, never from the tree)
pnpm prettier:check -> pnpm format:check -> pnpm quality-gate
the reviewer and the merge gate on the PR head
classes: C1 — the head carries no tracked path under .pair/red-snapshots/: the format gate lists nothing and exits 0 (origin/main is in this class)
C2 — the head carries exactly one manifest: the gate exits 1 naming that single path (the current defect, pr-0-a0.json)
C3 — the head carries several manifests (a multi-round cycle: pr-0-a0.json plus pr-494-r1-g1.json): every one of them must go, removing only the oldest is still the defect
C4 — the SNAPSHOT COMMIT itself carries the manifest: required, not a defect; verify reports manifest-missing-in-snapshot without it
C5 — no seal exists on the branch at all: the invariant holds vacuously and must not report a breach
interactions: I1 removal x custody — with every manifest deleted from the tree, verify/verify-chain still return verified:true, because the contract is read from the snapshot commit and the manifest path is filtered out of the post-seal delta

I2 deletion x fixScope.mode — the deletion's status is D and isModulePath('.pair/red-snapshots/…json') is true, so a BEHAVIORAL scope would make the fix itself a breach (behavioral-adds-or-moves-module, red-snapshot.mjs line 389). The scope must be structural; this is why the group's mode is not negotiable.

I3 removal x the gate's own file derivation — the invariant may be faked by hiding the path (gitignoring it, or adding a `.pair/` arm to git-tracked-paths.sh's case) instead of removing the file; both would silence the gate while leaving the defect
